The Delhi Police have registered an FIR against advocate Prashant Bhushan over the alleged circulation of a doctored video of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, which purportedly showed him criticising India over its internal affairs and oil purchases.
The case was registered by the Special Cell after the police came across claims about the video during cyber patrolling on November 3, according to a post by the Delhi Police on X.
The FIR was booked under Section 336(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with forgery intended to harm a person’s reputation; Section 353(1)(c), which penalises the circulation of statements or false information intended, or likely, to incite one class or community to commit an offence against another; Section 356, which deals with defamation; and Section 340(2), which penalises the fraudulent or dishonest use of a forged document or electronic record as genuine. The police have also invoked Section 66C of the Information Technology Act, which deals with identity theft, including the fraudulent or dishonest use of another person’s electronic signature, password or other unique identification feature.
According to the police, the matter came to their notice after the social media handle @thequotesnews claimed that a purportedly doctored video of Mr. Lavrov, allegedly hostile to India, had been shared from Mr. Bhushan’s handle, @pbhushan1 .
The police said the video was alleged to contain “misleading, defamatory, and inflammatory content to incite public disturbance and spread rumors”.
The registration of the FIR follows warnings from government fact-checking authorities and the Russian Embassy that the video was fabricated. The Ministry of External Affairs’ Fact Check unit had flagged the clip on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), stating that the video of the Russian Foreign Minister being circulated in the post was fake.
The Russian Embassy also rejected the remarks attributed to Mr. Lavrov, confirming that the video was fabricated.
Mr. Bhushan had shared the clip on social media, presenting the purported exchange as a “tight slap” against the Indian government. The video allegedly portrayed Mr. Lavrov as criticising India’s domestic affairs and its purchases of Russian oil.
Government fact-checking agencies subsequently clarified that the clip had been digitally altered, with fabricated audio and captions.
